svg.title: One key, four threads: what the GIL actually costs
svg.desc: Four thread boxes reaching for a single hachured key labelled GIL, with only one holding it. Beside them, one core interleaving jobs A B C D versus four cores running A, B, C and D genuinely at once. Below, a two-by-four grid of measured results shows threads making a CPU-bound workload 0.86 times as fast, circled in red, while asyncio makes an I/O-bound workload 27.02 times faster, circled in green. An Amdahl curve shows 95% parallel code flattening at about 16.8x even on a hundred cores.
svg.text: One key, four threads: what the GIL actually costs
one worker, four jobs in flight
four workers, genuinely at the same time
released on I/O and every 5 ms - NOT while you are computing.
SLOWER than doing nothing at all
threads will speed up my CPU loop
0.86x. Contention costs more than the GIL saves.
you cannot concurrency your way out of arithmetic.
Amdahl: at 95% parallel, 20 cores buys 10.3x and 100 buys 16.8x
